summary: A high-quality IELTS Academic paper: three passages of 856-899 words, rising from a history of street lighting to a demanding psychology argument about procrastination, with well-paraphrased questions. One pair of True/False/Not Given questions was out of passage order and has been swapped; nothing else needed fixing.
strengths: Passage 3 is genuinely C1: abstract argument, metaphor ('a loan at high interest', 'the emotional cliff') and evidence from several research traditions.
Questions paraphrase rather than copy (valid reason / without good reason; groups / clusters; pardons / forgiving themselves; no clear starting point / no obvious first move).
Passage 2 matching-people task has a genuine extra name (Jonas Berg) and the summary follows passage order.
MCQ distractors are plausible and some reverse the text (Q27 D, Q28 B), as in the real test.

issues.problem: T/F/NG out of passage order: Q8 (Paris lanterns, paragraph 2) came before Q9 (link-boys, paragraph 1).
issues.change: Swapped the statements: Q8 = link-boys earnings (NOT GIVEN), Q9 = Paris lanterns paid by householders (FALSE). Keys now T, NG, F, T, T, F, NG.

issues.problem: Q4 repeats the passage word for word ('lit each lamp high above the street with long').
issues.change: Suggest 'Lamplighters reached the lamps with the help of long ______.'

issues.problem: Summary gaps 20 and 21 keep the passage's collocations ('strong winds', 'safe landing sites'), so they are easy to locate.
issues.change: Acceptable; for a harder version use 'in gusty ______' and 'places where drones can safely ______'.
